title: The Evening Brief: Injuries reshape NFL; Lakers sale clears $12.5B record
dek: The NFL preseason weekend produced cascading injury updates that will shape roster decisions through the regular season, while a landmark ownership sale and high-profile retirements marked major business milestones across sports.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Ricky Pearsall's season-ending knee surgery targeting a 2027 return is the most consequential NFL roster decision of the preseason; the 49ers now absorb his absence for all of 2026 after an initial bid to rehab conservatively failed when swelling emerged during training camp.
bottom_line: The NFL preseason weekend reshaped rosters through injury decisions that will define the regular season: Pearsall's surgery ends the 49ers' 2026 at receiver, Beck's precautionary rest buys Arizona time, and Allen's full health clears Buffalo to move forward. A record Lakers sale, Westbrook's retirement, Skip Bertman's death, and escalating FIFA governance battles marked major business and personnel milestones across sports. Watch for Pearsall's recovery timeline updates, Allen's actual playing time Saturday, the Lakers sale's September board approval, and whether Infantino faces a credible challenger by November 18.
body: The NFL preseason brought a succession of injury decisions that will echo through the regular season. The 49ers' Ricky Pearsall underwent PCL repair surgery and is targeting a nine-month recovery before the 2027 season, per the desk's reporting. The timeline marks a pivotal moment for the receiver: he initially suffered the knee injury in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville last season and cost him all or parts of 10 games, and the 49ers had opted against surgery in the offseason hoping rehabilitation would suffice. Swelling that developed during training camp forced the surgical decision and season-ending injured reserve placement. Pearsall has appeared in only 20 games across three NFL seasons, including a robbery-related injury that cost him his first six games as a rookie.

Across the NFL, other injury moves unfolded with less finality. Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck sustained a rib injury during the Hall of Fame Game in the first quarter but continued playing and gained a first down on the play that hurt him. Team sources told ESPN the injury is not serious and carries zero long-term concern, though the Cardinals are holding him out of Thursday's preseason game against Las Vegas as a precaution. Buffalo's Josh Allen remains fully healthy and will play Saturday's preseason opener at the new Highmark Stadium against Carolina, head coach Joe Brady announced, marking Allen's first preseason action since 2024.

Preseason team conduct also made news. Philadelphia's Moro Ojomo and Fred Johnson fought during Thursday's final practice before Saturday's preseason opener against Baltimore, with the altercation escalating from a late shove into punches and a diving tackle. Coaches separated both players, and general manager Howie Roseman and head coach Nick Sirianni met with them individually. Both remained on the roster heading into the Ravens game.

Outside football, the Lakers sale to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at $12.5 billion marks a record valuation for a professional sports franchise. Mark Walter took controlling interest in October 2025 at roughly $10 billion; the agreed price reflects a roughly 25 percent increase in under a year. The sale still requires NBA board of governors approval, with the board next meeting in September. In basketball, Russell Westbrook announced his retirement after 18 seasons, leaving as the NBA's all-time triple-double leader with 209, along with 27,176 points and 10,351 assists across 1,301 games for seven franchises.

College baseball lost a landmark figure when Skip Bertman, who built LSU into a dynasty with five national titles and 870 wins, died Friday at 88. Bertman later served as LSU's athletic director during football national championships in 2003 and 2007. In soccer, Zinedine Zidane appointed Fabien Barthez as France's goalkeeper coach, reuniting the World Cup-winning pair as Zidane builds his backroom staff for Nations League fixtures beginning in September. Celta Vigo's season-opening La Liga match against Osasuna was postponed from August 17 to August 27 after a fungal outbreak made the pitch at Estadio de Balaidos unfit for play, though Osasuna disputed the rescheduling decision, saying both clubs had agreed to move the match to the international break instead.

In swimming, Katie Ledecky extended her 1,500 freestyle winning streak to 16 years with a victory in 15:36.09 at the Pan Pacific Championships in Irvine, holding off Australia's Lani Pallister in her closest finish in 13 years. A U.S. quartet of Will Modglin, Van Mathias, Gretchen Walsh and Kate Douglass lowered the mixed medley relay world record to 3:36.70, bettering the previous mark of 3:37.43 set by an American team in 2024. In soccer governance, six Arab football federations publicly backed FIFA President Gianni Infantino on Thursday as he navigates organized opposition to his withdrawn $20 billion World Cup privatization proposal. UEFA, CONCACAF, and AFC issued a joint letter condemning the proposal as a fundamental breach of trust, while England, Wales, and Ireland withdrew support for his reelection in 2027. Infantino's regional coalition buys him time and votes ahead of the November 18 challenger deadline and March 2027 election in Morocco. In trading cards, Panini escalated its three-year antitrust case against Fanatics by alleging the rival obtained granular details of Panini's existing deals, royalty rates, minimum guarantee schedules, marketing commitments, and autograph spend obligations, and used that information to secure exclusive NBA and NFL card licenses.
